name: Merge queue in both loop scripts
goal: Both loop scripts squash the finished branches one after another in the main checkout: they accept SLICE-READY, merge each branch, commit with the message from the file, tick Commit, remove the merged branch and worktree, and stop with the file names on any conflict; --merge runs that queue alone.
scope: assets/slice-loop.sh and assets/slice-loop.ps1, functionally identical: a build turn that ends in `SLICE-READY: NN` (besides `SLICE-DONE: NN`) hands the slice to the merge queue

Merge queue: in the main checkout, with a clean working tree, `git merge --squash slice-NN`; on any conflict reset the merge (`git reset --merge`), keep the branch, report the conflicted files (`git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`) and exit 1

Commit: tick the Commit column of row NN in work/checklist.md, stage, `git commit -F .slice-loop/slice-NN.msg`; when the file is missing, write `Slice NN: <name> (<source>)` from work/_slices.json to a temporary file and use that with -F (F-08); then the usual is_done check
Cleanup: `git worktree remove <path>` without `--force` when `git worktree list --porcelain` shows the branch, then `git branch -d slice-NN`; a worktree that cannot be removed is reported and left
`--parallel` / `-Parallel`: builds run side by side, squashes run one after another in the main process in finishing order

`--merge` / `-Merge`: squash every branch slice-NN whose checklist row on the branch (`git show slice-NN:work/checklist.md`) has every column but Commit ticked, lowest number first, then exit 0 without starting a session; works without an open round

name: Command rules: assumptions, seams, tests, stop criteria, review axes, ADR, debugging
goal: The /slice command tells a session how to plan assumptions, cut and verify tests, when to stop, how to review and when an ADR is due, in nine short positive sentences, so sessions stop asking one question at a time, writing tautological tests and stopping for trivia.
scope: references/slice-command.md section 3, plan: assumptions as one numbered round with a recommendation per point, worded so that 'yes' takes the recommendations; facts come from code and docs, only decisions are asked; an unambiguous task skips the round (F-09.1)
Section 3, plan: name the seams the tests hit; the review focus says per seam what the test catches and what it misses (F-09.2)

Section 3, tests first: expected values from an independent source, never computed like the code (no tautological tests); red counts only when the test checks exactly the fault or requirement; type check and the single test file often, the full suite once at the end; refactor after green (F-09.3)

Section 3, build: stop only for a real blocker – missing dependency, contradiction to the plan, an ambiguity that would produce wrong code under a wrong assumption; trivia the code answers, style questions (follow existing patterns) and things a test can settle go on; no 'subagent or inline?' question after the plan (F-09.4)

Section 4, review on two separate axes: specification – every finding cites the plan line, unrequested scope is asked about – and standards – the repository rule beats the general rule, what tools enforce stays out (F-09.5)
Section 4, before the squash (and before SLICE-READY once slice 03 adds it): merge the integration branch into slice-NN and run the checks after the merge; extends the F-03 line of slice 01 (F-09.6)
Section 4, decisions: an ADR only when the decision is hard to reverse, would surprise without context or settled a real conflict of goals; everything else is a Ruling in the round record (F-09.7)
